comments.text: Resident scene-request prefix, retained byte-for-byte from the opening snapshot across $59AF-$59DB. Read queued cell request $02C3. A negative byte skips conversion. For a nonnegative queued byte, if pending scene $0530 is negative, copy the queued byte there; a copied nonzero scene with entry $0532=$FF receives default entry1. Clear any consumed nonnegative queued request to $FF, including one displaced by an existing pending request. Then $59D1 tests the pending request. Live controlled phase4 guard departures have queued5/pendingFF/entryFF before this service and reach loader $5098 with pending5/entry1/queuedFF. This bounds the request hand-off, not the full loader or destination mechanics.

Negative pending scene skips the load at $59E9. Nonnegative pending scene calls wheel closer $60E6 then loader $5098. The page's bounded function checks byte values with both side effects intercepted, stopping at $59DC on the load path or $59E9 on the no-load path. The separate VICE trials complete the real loads and arrive in scene5 at X84/depth6.
ASK ALPH action/object pair [30,44]. Parallel pointer $8BCC selects $8FA8. Live dispatch reached that handler three times after CALL ALPH beside the left door in a forced scene-four reference state.
ASK RALPH action/object pair [30,53]. Parallel pointer $8BD4 selects $8FAE. Live fresh-room and switched-speaker trials reached that handler three and one times respectively beside the right door.
CALL ALPH action/object pair [31,44], with parallel pointer $8BDC selecting $90C3.
CALL RALPH action/object pair [31,53]. Parallel pointer $8BE8 selects $90CC. Both right-door trials recorded one call-handler hit.
Pointer to $8FA8 for the ASK ALPH pair at $8B0C.
Pointer to ASK RALPH $8FAE, paired with $8B14. It uses Ralph's presence prerequisite before joining the same conversation as ASK ALPH.
Pointer to CALL ALPH handler $90C3.
Pointer to CALL RALPH $90CC. The checked call preserves the shared opening conversation index, including index1 after Alph's first reply.

Reached from the room callback when depth is at least40 and no entry countdown is active. For column $AF=1, zero selector $8F06 jumps to $8EAE; nonzero continues $8DF8. For every other column, nonzero jumps to $8EAE and zero continues. The controlled left-door snapshot has column1/selector1. Ordinary up input from its opened door reached the continuation, displayed How did she figure it out, advanced phase1 to2 and loaded scene5 The Wall of Hands. In the same selector1 setup, ordinary right-door entry at column3 reached $8EAE and the loss sequence. The setup prefix at $8F15 generates the selector once while its guard is negative. Complete ordinary return visits and other recorded playthroughs remain open.

If message flag $8F0B is nonnegative, skip to $8E59. Otherwise compare depth $0544 with $8F0E; below threshold also skips. Negative remembered selection $8F0A chooses generic reaction $9C9A. Nonnegative selection is XOR1 and stored as speaker $8F05, then the phase dispatch follows. Live controlled phase4 left-door entry checks unselected, congratulated-Alph/second0 and congratulated-Alph/second1 states. Their retained thresholds are40/44; ordinary phase4 arrival remains open.

Arrive with phase in A. A=4 compares remembered selection $8F0A with second random bit $8F07. Equal selects $9DC9 (other guard says the selected guard always lies); different selects $9E10 (tells the truth). Other A retains the incoming text pointer; the page models only phase4 and leaves phase2/3 dispatch separate.

Negative remembered selection selects $9C9A, How did she figure it out, in the female-avatar image. This path preserves existing speaker selector $8F05. Live unselected phase4 doorway trial checks that generic reply.

Zero speaker selector calls $93EA; nonzero calls $9407. Both preserve X/Y, then $9419 queues the selected text. Store0 at message flag $8F0B afterward. The phase4 selected-Alph trials set speaker1 via XOR1 and use the other-guard helper. Speaker selection and output arguments are checked against original code; complete animation semantics remain open.

Independently compare depth $0544 with countdown threshold $8F0F. Below threshold returns. At least threshold clears $02BB and outcome $8F0D, and stores9 at countdown $8F10. This runs even when the message gate skipped. The controlled doorway trials retain thresholds40/44 and continue up until the actual initializer before releasing input. These are stored depth bytes, not a wall-clock duration.

Entry countdown callback reached with A holding the old $8F10. Decrement $8F10; old A8 requests sound1 and returns, old6 requests sound13 and returns. Other old values read the decremented count; nonzero returns. At zero, nonzero $8F0D jumps to $8EC1; the controlled right-door route takes that losing sequence. Zero $8F0D requests sound14, waits through $0839 with Y4, stores5 at $02C3 and advances phase through $8E9E. The controlled left-door entry used the zero outcome byte, completed this path once, and reached the scene5 loader. Countdown calls are not assigned a wall-clock rate here.

Increment $056A modulo256. If the resulting byte is at least5, store4; otherwise retain it. Ordinary opened-left-door entry from the controlled phase1 room passed here once, then the loader selected scene5 and the Wall of Hands arrival was captured. The isolated test checks every phase byte; arbitrary wrap states are not gameplay reachability claims.

Alternate entry selected by $8DDF. Set $02BB=0, outcome $8F0D=1, request sound1 via $081E, then set countdown $8F10=9. Ordinary up through the opened right door at column3 with selector1 reached this routine in the controlled count15/phase1 room. This is one captured selector setup, not a fixed right-door outcome in every playthrough.

Called when $8E70 decrements the entry countdown to zero with nonzero outcome $8F0D. Request sound18, queue $9E68 with A6, wait through $0839/Y10, request sound16, clear the message area via $0836, wait with Y3, queue $9E97 with A2 and wait with Y5. Set $0580=1 and request description $9F44 with A=$FF through $0857. Captured right-door route displayed the falling/lied messages then the loss panel; phase1 and scene4 persisted through the recorded loss. Delay arguments are not a measured wall-clock duration.

Setup guard read by $8F15: nonnegative returns immediately; negative runs the initialization prefix and is changed to0 before command availability is installed and two random bits are stored. The saved controlled loader-return state has FF; the ordinary callback ran the prefix once and left0. After240 no-input frames both bits were unchanged while the random state advanced. Reset on a complete ordinary revisit remains open.

Shared mutable conversation index used by Alph and Ralph. Below count15, opening indices0,1,2 advance0 to1 to2 to2. Calling Ralph preserves it. After acknowledged count15 in phase1, $9004 increments then retains1 when old0; otherwise decrements back to the old byte and selects a detail reply. The controlled post-thanks trial kept2 through three asks. Higher phases remain open.

One-byte selector for room speech: accepted Alph prerequisite sets0, Ralph sets1. In the entry reaction a nonnegative remembered selection is XOR1 into this byte so the other guard speaks; a negative selection leaves it unchanged. The phase4 page uses valid remembered selections0/1 and the negative $FF case.

First stored random bit, written by $8F2C as A AND1 after $0821 advances the random generator. Entry choice $8DDF continues for column1/nonzero or another column/zero, and takes the losing branch for the opposite combinations. Both recorded door traversals use value1. Controlled initializer trials with seeds0 and7 stored0 and1. These are seed-poked comparisons, not ordinary routes selecting a preferred bit. Later writes/initialization on ordinary return visits remain open.

One bit stored by the second setup random call. Later ASK $90A6 compares it with $8F06 for castle/death wording. CONGRATULATE $911D compares it with selected speaker $8F05 for lying/truth wording after phase4 and asked-flag checks. The remaining literal read at $8E2C belongs to a departure reaction whose complete route remains open.

One-byte flag set to1 by $909D for speaker selector0 at the capped later ASK. CONGRATULATE reads it at $910D in phase4: zero queues the haven't-done-anything reply; nonzero permits role wording and selection at $911A.

One-byte flag set to1 by $90A3 for nonzero speaker selector at the capped later ASK. CONGRATULATE reads it at $9115 in phase4, with zero refusing and nonzero permitting $911A. Original-code checks cover this branch; live congratulations trials use Alph.

One byte written at $911A with the accepted phase4 congratulated speaker after its asked flag is nonzero and conversation flag is nonnegative. At $8E05 negative takes the generic entry reaction. Nonnegative selection XOR1 chooses the other speaker; phase4 compares the original selection with $8F07 for lying/truth wording. Live controlled Alph selection0 trials check both second-bit values; ordinary phase4 arrival and live Ralph departure remain open.

One-byte entry-reaction gate read at $8DF8. Negative permits a reply once depth reaches $8F0E; successful queue clears it to0 at $8E56. The callback below depth40 writes $FF at $8DD7. The page checks the full byte domain at the reaction gate; complete revisit behavior remains open.

One-byte conversation flag. INSULT stores $FF at $9151. CONGRATULATE sees a negative byte, clears it to0 and queues the fickle reply before other checks. ASK also reads it at $8FB1; full ordinary reset/persistence behavior remains open.

One-byte depth threshold compared at $8E00. The saved controlled trials retain40 from the earlier room setup. Setup code $8F3E-$8F40 writes54 when its entry phase is at least2; full ordinary phase4 initialization is not claimed by the later snapshot trials.

One-byte depth threshold compared at $8E5C. The saved trials retain44. Setup code $8F43-$8F45 writes64 for entry phase at least2; the controlled later-phase snapshots did not rerun that setup. Reaching this threshold initializes the successful nine-count sequence at $8E61-$8E6B.

Mutable local byte read by phase1 conversation at $9018, incremented by a changing phase1 OPEN at $92CC and decremented by a changing CLOSE at $9292. Controlled room's initial FF became0 on ordinary left-door OPEN, then FF on CLOSE. ASK replies changed Figure it out for yourself to the unsure response and back while Brick Hallway count15 stayed fixed. This establishes the local cycle, not initialization/persistence or all door outcomes.

Return when $8F03 is nonnegative. Otherwise store0 there, pass X=$84/Y=$9F to command-availability API $0833, call random API $0821, mask A to bit0 and store $8F06, call it again and store bit0 at $8F07. $0821 returns the high byte of the updated 16-bit state at $0502/$0503: new=(37*old+17) modulo65536. The page/test starts from the state before these two generator calls. The following $8F37 prefix sets depth thresholds for phases at least2; the remaining tail from $8F48 is unanalysed here; the second bit chooses the later castle/death answer at $90A6.

Compare entry phase $056A with2 using unsigned carry. Values0/1 preserve existing thresholds;2..255 write54 to reaction depth $8F0E and64 to countdown depth $8F0F, then fall through $8F48. All256 phase bytes are checked against this original prefix, stopping at $8F48. The live later-phase snapshots changed phase after setup and retain40/44; they are not a complete phase4 initialization check.

Call prerequisite $939A, then join $8FB1. Ordinary ASK ALPH at X99/depth6 after CALL ALPH reached the first three conversation replies. The source snapshot was reached by a forced scene request, not a verified crossing from the Brick Hallway.

Call Ralph prerequisite $93B7, then join shared conversation $8FB1. Compare opened-door counter $0569 with15. Below15 branches to opening replies at $8FE5. Tail jump to $9419 with selected message Y/X. The queue loads speaker mode from $0342. Does not itself change phase or acknowledgement.

For valid old index3, different selects $9B92 (certain death), equal selects $9B73 (castle). This comparison does not read the speaker selector. The byte-domain behavior outside valid shared indices is not modelled by the page.

Five high bytes for reply pointers, indexed by Y; low bytes start at $90BE. Entries are $9A11,$9CB6,$9CE3,$9B92,$9B73. The first three are fixed replies; the final two share capped conversation index3.

You don't have to shout! and preserved the index.

Compare that value with second random bit $8F07: equal selects $9D2C (Thanks, I think I lie pretty well); different selects $9D52 (Yes, telling the truth's a virtue). INSULT RALPH and HIT RALPH share this handler; it calls the existing Ralph prerequisite and falls through to $9148. Original-code tests check the accepted presence branch; a live Ralph route remains open.

Queue $9E58 through the speaker output helper, then store $FF at $8F0C. A following accepted CONGRATULATE clears that byte and selects the fickle reply before checking phase or asked flags. Original-code checks retain this order and its output request.

CLOSE DOOR pair [32,45] at $8B30 points here through $8BF0. Require a nonzero map type through $941F, retaining cell nibble A and column Y. At depth at least25 queue $9EBA. Otherwise compare closing replacement $072E+cellNibble with the old nibble; equal queues already-closed $952F. A change decrements $8F13 modulo256, calls mutation API $081B, then sound2. Load close replacement indexed by original cell nibble. If different, decrement local flag $8F13 before mutation $081B and sound2; otherwise queue $952F with mode5. The tested ordinary left-door change was2 to1, flag0 toFF.

Compare opening replacement $071E+cellNibble to old nibble; equality queues $9519. If different and phase $056A=1, increment local flag $8F13 and override replacement to2 or3 according to column Y and $8F06. Other phases use the table replacement. At depth6 the command dispatched but selected You're not close enough and made no mutation. Later phase semantics and ordinary room entry remain open.

Increment $8F13 modulo256 on a changing phase1 OPEN. If Y=1 choose3 when $8F06=0, otherwise2. If Y differs from1 choose2 when $8F06=0, otherwise3. The captured left door uses Y1 and $8F06=1, producing cell2. The type tests, door outcomes and meaning of this selector outside the checked sequence remain open.

Apply the selected replacement through $081B then request sound1 through $081E. The original mutation refreshed the left doorway and retained current scene4; it did not change Brick Hallway count $0569.

Query $93D1; negative uses the shared stack-discard return. Zero starts $93EA and queues $99FB through the rejection path. Nonzero starts $9407 and selects speaker1 at $8F05. Accepted Ralph and Alph presence paths are checked with API $0812 returning zero distance and $053E seeded1/0 respectively, matching the controlled door-side states. This isolated check does not model the distance producer. Live Ralph asks beside the right door continued into the shared opening conversation.
Call API $0812. Returned A at least30 queues $94EE with mode4 and returns $FF. Otherwise return $053E. The producer/meaning of the API's distance and actor state is outside this partial check.
Preserve A; set $0341 to5, $0342 to6 when player-column scratch $AF equals1 or zero otherwise, and $8F01 to12. Restore A. The controlled left-door CALL ALPH made the character appear.
Preserve A; set $0341 to7, $0342 to32 and $8F02 to12, then restore A. The complete animation consumer remains unannotated.

Headered first opening reply. Original parser expansion: One door leads to the center of the Labyrinth, the other leads to... CERTAIN DEATH! Live ASK ALPH displayed it after CALL ALPH beside the left door.

Phase4 remembered selection equal to second bit selects this record.
